title: a LevelSequence with tracks and keyframes
proves: author a sequence with bindings, tracks and keys, read it back, place it in the level and play it

editor.reason: install gate refused; no editor was contacted

install_gate.reason: Set MCP_UNREAL_PROJECT_ROOT to the test project root

steps.label: primitive puerts_sequence_build is NOT usable
steps.detail: not registered and not in the tool inventory
steps.why: create or update a LevelSequence: frame rate, playback range, actor bindings, tracks and keyframes. No registered tool touches Sequencer at all. The only LevelSequence code in the repository (generation/sequence_generator.py) creates an empty asset and sets its playback range, is reachable only through the legacy prompt_generate pipeline, and writes no track, no section and no key

steps.label: primitive puerts_sequence_inspect is NOT usable
steps.detail: not registered and not in the tool inventory
steps.why: read a LevelSequence back as machine-readable JSON: bindings, tracks, sections, keyframe times and values, and a structure hash. Required by the builder-plus-inspector rule every other builder in this bridge follows, and without it a keyframe claim cannot be verified without a human opening Sequencer

steps.label: primitive puerts_scene_batch is NOT usable
steps.detail: not registered and not in the tool inventory
steps.why: place a LevelSequenceActor that points at the sequence. puerts_spawn_actor can spawn the actor class but cannot set its LevelSequence property or label it

steps.label: primitive puerts_sequence_render is NOT usable
steps.detail: not registered and not in the tool inventory
steps.why: render a LevelSequence to image frames or a video so the result of a cinematic prompt can be looked at. puerts_viewport_screenshot captures one editor viewport frame and cannot follow a sequence's camera cuts

steps.label: 1. build the intro sequence with two bound tracks and five keys
2. read the sequence back and count the keys that actually landed
3. place a LevelSequenceActor that points at it
4. render the three seconds so the result can be looked at
5. what this slice is really reporting
steps.detail: cinematics is the only one of the seven domains with no owner and no partial support. Four primitives are missing and three of them are unowned. The nearest existing code, title_sequence_bind, writes a JSON scaffold and its own runtime_note says a dedicated Sequencer bridge tool is required.

proposed_schema.owner: UNOWNED. No lane in this program covers Sequencer

params.tracks: [{binding: id|'master', type:'Transform'|'Float'|'Visibility'|'Event'|'Camera'|'Audio', property?: 'RelativeLocation'|..., sections: [{start_frame, end_frame, keys: [{frame, value, interpolation:'Linear'|'Cubic'|'Constant'}]}]}]

proposed_schema.note: UE4.27 API surface for this is ULevelSequence, UMovieScene::AddTrack / AddPossessable, UMovieScene3DTransformTrack and FMovieSceneDoubleChannel-era FMovieSceneFloatChannel. All editor C++, so it belongs in MCPBridgeGraphBuilder next to the other builders.

proposed_schema.returns: { frame_rate, playback_range, bindings, tracks: [{binding, type, property, sections: [{start_frame, end_frame, keys}]}], structure_hash_sha1, package_dirty_before, package_dirty_after }

proposed_schema.note: UE4.27 ships Movie Render Queue as a plugin; the fallback is the older FSequencerRenderer / automated level sequence capture path. Which one is available is a project-settings question, so the tool must report which it used.
